claims.text: MnNiSi-based compounds can exhibit a large magnetocaloric response but comparatively poor mechanical ductility or fracture toughness.
Replacing approximately 5–10% of the Ni-site atoms with Co will improve the mechanical performance of MnNiSi.
Co substitutes specifically on the Ni crystallographic site in Mn(Ni1-xCox)Si.
Co substitution enhances lattice cohesion in MnNiSi.
Co substitution improves the grain-boundary structure of MnNiSi.
Co incorporation modifies metallic bonding and microstructure in a way that improves toughness and ductility.
The bonding and microstructural changes caused by Co increase resistance to crack initiation and propagation.
Moderate Co substitution preserves the magnetic ordering responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Mn(Ni1-xCox)Si with x approximately 0.05–0.10 will have higher fracture toughness or ductility than undoped MnNiSi.
Mn(Ni1-xCox)Si with x approximately 0.05–0.10 will retain magnetocaloric entropy and adiabatic-temperature changes comparable to those of undoped MnNiSi under the same field conditions.
The proposed combination of improved mechanics and retained magnetocaloric performance is expected to hold for Co substitution levels up to approximately 10%.
Co substitution above approximately 10% could cause segregation or phase separation.
Segregation or phase separation could degrade both mechanical and magnetocaloric properties.
Poor processing control could degrade both mechanical and magnetocaloric properties.
Homogeneous elemental distribution under processing conditions comparable to the baseline is required for the hypothesis to hold.

contradictions.description: The synthesis is described as occurring at ambient temperature while also requiring controlled thermal processing; without clarification, these processing conditions are internally inconsistent.
